clue.text: Momentous heart?

parts.note: surface reading: a hugely significant moment
setter's reading: what happens to the word heart when its letters are broken up and rearranged into the planet's name

explanation.surface: A heart described as momentous, perhaps one beating at a great occasion.
explanation.walkthrough: Shatter the letters of HEART and you get EARTH, so HEART is literally EARTH-SHATTERING; the question mark flags the pun.
explanation.definitionFit: Something earth-shattering is of enormous importance, the idiom for a momentous event.

clue.text: Odd enchantress, rising to ensnare copper

indicators.note: to ensnare is to trap inside, so the coin sits within the reversed name

parts.note: Circe is the enchantress of Greek myth who turned Odysseus's men into pigs
a cent is an American copper coin

explanation.surface: A strange sorceress ascending to catch a policeman.
explanation.walkthrough: Copper looks like the police officer or the metal; here it is a one-cent coin.
explanation.definitionFit: Eccentric means unconventional and strange, which is what odd means of a person.

clue.text: Feeling sorry for everyone (including children) after destruction

indicators.note: after places the rating behind the word for destruction

parts.note: ruin means destruction
G is the American film rating for general audiences, suitable for all ages

explanation.surface: Pity for all, children included, in the aftermath of a disaster.
explanation.walkthrough: G is the US film rating meaning suitable for everyone.
explanation.definitionFit: Ruing is regretting, the present participle of rue, so it matches feeling sorry.

clue.text: Infusion distressed the bear

indicators.note: distressed means upset or roughed up, so the letters are thrown into disorder

parts.note: taken as written

explanation.surface: A soothing brew for a bear in a state of anxiety.
explanation.definitionFit: An infusion is a drink made by steeping leaves in hot water, as with chamomile or mint tisane.

clue.text: Greeting very quiet orange beast

parts.note: hi is a greeting
pp, pianissimo, is the musical marking for very quiet

parts.note: the first letter of orange

explanation.surface: A hushed hello to an orange animal, perhaps an orangutan or a tiger.
explanation.walkthrough: The wordplay is HI + PP + O; the O comes from the initial of orange, a light touch rather than a stated indicator.
explanation.definitionFit: The hippo, short for hippopotamus, is a large African animal, a beast.

clue.text: Gets ready to run away, reciting something Chaucer might have written about a seabird?

indicators.note: reciting is speaking out loud, so the answer is heard rather than seen

parts.words: something Chaucer might have written about a seabird
parts.note: Chaucer wrote The Canterbury Tales, each one 'The X's Tale', and a tern is a seabird

explanation.surface: A nervous poet preparing to flee while reciting a medieval verse about a seagull.
explanation.walkthrough: Chaucer's tales are titled like The Knight's Tale, so a seabird's story would be The Tern's Tale.
explanation.definitionFit: To turn tail is the idiom for fleeing, turning one's back to run off.

clue.text: Mathematical figure otherwise circumscribing edge

indicators.note: circumscribing means drawing a line around, so one word encloses the other

parts.note: else means otherwise
a lip is an edge or rim

explanation.surface: Geometry jargon: some shape drawn around a border.
explanation.walkthrough: Circumscribing is a real geometry term, which makes it look like part of the definition.
explanation.definitionFit: An ellipse is an oval curve, a conic section studied in geometry.

clue.text: Orgiastic romp with titan of great consequence

indicators.note: an orgiastic party is wild and unrestrained, so these letters are thrown about

parts.note: taken as written
taken as written

explanation.surface: A wild party with a powerful figure, a scandal of real significance.
explanation.definitionFit: Important means significant, mattering a great deal, which is to be of great consequence.

clue.text: Participant in rogue's shindig: One can be educated or wild

definitions.text: One can be educated or wild

indicators.note: a participant is part of an event, so the answer is a part of the following words

parts.note: the letters run across the end of rogue's and the start of shindig

explanation.surface: Someone at a scoundrel's party could be cultured or unruly.
explanation.walkthrough: The definition plays on two fixed phrases, an educated guess and a wild guess.
explanation.definitionFit: Both familiar phrases pair these adjectives with a single noun for an estimate made without certainty.

clue.text: Essential energy reflected the sound of a cat and the sound of a bird

parts.note: chi is the vital life force in Chinese philosophy

indicators.note: a reflection in a mirror shows things back to front, so the word that follows is read right to left

parts.note: a contented cat purrs

explanation.surface: A nature recording of essential sounds: a cat and a bird, echoing back.
explanation.walkthrough: Essential energy is the Chinese concept of life force, not a physics term; only the cat's sound is reflected, not the energy.
explanation.definitionFit: A chirrup is a short repeated chirp, the twittering call of a small songbird.

clue.text: Backslide and return psychic's gift with warning, mostly

indicators.note: mostly means not quite all, so the last letter of the warning word is dropped
to return is to go back, so the whole combination is read from the end to the start

parts.note: ESP, extrasensory perception, is the gift a psychic claims
an alert is a warning; mostly drops its final letter

explanation.surface: A sceptic, tired of a fortune-teller's predictions, wants to give the gift back with a caution.
explanation.walkthrough: ESP plus ALER makes ESPALER, which read backwards is RELAPSE.
explanation.definitionFit: To relapse is to slip back into a former, worse state, which is what backsliding means.

clue.text: No! A thousand times no! Teasing is unacceptable!

indicators.note: something unacceptable in its present state must be changed, so these letters are rearranged

parts.note: the opening word taken as written
taken as written

explanation.surface: An outraged protest that being teased is simply not on.
explanation.walkthrough: The opening No is not exclamation but fodder; the definition is the emphatic refusal that follows it, a thousand noes.
explanation.definitionFit: Saying no over and over amounts to a string of refusals, that is, many denials.

clue.text: Mona Lisa's home is beyond standard

indicators.note: beyond means further along, so this small word is placed after the golf term

parts.note: par is the standard, as in up to par
taken as written

explanation.surface: A claim that the Mona Lisa's gallery is above the usual level.
explanation.walkthrough: 'is beyond standard' places IS after PAR.
explanation.definitionFit: The Mona Lisa hangs in the Louvre, the museum in the French capital.

clue.text: Between drinks, sorcerer's way to make money

indicators.note: between puts the sorcerer's word in the gap separating two drinks

parts.note: rum is a drink, the first of the pair
a mage is a sorcerer, with the possessive s kept
ale is a drink, the second of the pair

explanation.surface: A wizard who earns a living between rounds at the pub.
explanation.walkthrough: The single word drinks has to supply two different drinks, one on each side of the sorcerer.
explanation.definitionFit: A rummage sale sells donated second-hand goods to raise funds, typically for a charity or church.

clue.text: Salmon I'd cooked holding unknown instruments

indicators.note: holding means keeping inside, so the unknown sits within the mixture
cooked means altered or doctored, so the letters are rearranged

parts.note: taken as written
n is a mathematical unknown

explanation.surface: A chef boasts of cooking salmon that contains a mystery ingredient.
explanation.walkthrough: The N added to the fodder is the algebraic unknown.
explanation.definitionFit: Mandolins are stringed instruments of the lute family, plucked with a pick.

clue.text: Engineer overlooking crazy impression

indicators.note: in a down clue overlooking means sitting above, so this abbreviation comes first

parts.note: Eng. is the abbreviation for engineer
raving means crazy, as in raving mad

explanation.surface: An engineer ignoring a mad notion.
explanation.walkthrough: Overlooking seems to mean ignoring; it is positional, one piece above the other.
explanation.definitionFit: An engraving is a print made from an engraved plate, an impression taken in ink.

clue.text: Refuse destination, even after rejecting Teddy Roosevelt

indicators.note: rejecting someone throws them out, so his initials are removed from the start

parts.note: where rubbish goes in America

explanation.surface: Where a cartoonist might dump a portrait of a president.
explanation.walkthrough: The definition is used twice: a trash can minus TR is still a refuse destination, an ash can, hence 'even after'.
explanation.definitionFit: An ash can is an American dustbin, originally for fireplace ashes, so it is where rubbish ends up.

clue.text: Cheer up large bobtail horse with a clown

indicators.note: a bobtail is a docked tail, so the horse word loses its last letter

parts.note: rah is an American cheer, as in rah-rah

equine means horse; bobtail removes its final letter

explanation.surface: Trying to lift spirits with a big short-tailed horse and a circus clown.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Cheer up' looks like the definition, meaning to hearten; it is two instructions.
explanation.definitionFit: Harlequin is the masked comic servant of commedia dell'arte in a diamond-patterned costume, a stock clown figure.

clue.text: See 16
Elevated less serious reader's implement

parts.note: elevated means raised up, high
lighter in mood means less serious

explanation.surface: A reader's tool described as raised and more frivolous than before.
explanation.definitionFit: A highlighter is a fluorescent marker pen used by readers to pick out passages in a text.

clue.text: Something you could eat for breakfast: fish sandwiches, without a doctor's orders

definitions.text: Something you could eat for breakfast

indicators.note: to sandwich something is to put it between two halves, so the fish goes round the rest

parts.note: hake is a fish

explanation.surface: A breakfast of fish sandwiches eaten against medical advice.
explanation.walkthrough: Sandwiches is a verb here, not breakfast food.
explanation.definitionFit: A hotcake is a pancake, an American breakfast staple served in stacks.

clue.text: Former African strongman raised stipulation to put in silver

to add is to put in
Ag is the chemical symbol for silver

explanation.walkthrough: IF, ADD and AG are joined and then the whole string is read upwards.
explanation.definitionFit: Muammar Gaddafi ruled Libya as a dictator from 1969 until his death in 2011.

clue.text: Termination of ailment by licking a fish

parts.note: the final letter of ailment
a licking is a heavy defeat, a rout

explanation.definitionFit: A troop is a unit of soldiers, especially of cavalry, so the word stands for a body of them.

clue.text: Common bird, once carrying only letters from Singapore

parts.words: Common bird, once carrying only letters
parts.note: surface reading: a bird that used to carry nothing but mail, like a carrier pigeon
setter's reading: every letter of the answer can be found in the word Singapore

explanation.walkthrough: The answer is the extinct North American bird, and it is spelt using only S, I, N, G, A, P, O, R and E.
